tspan.tspan: Secondary use of heterogeneous clinical data requires consistent, reusable representations. HL7 Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (FHIR) profiles specify
constraints on resource structure, cardinalities, and terminology. [1] However, transformation pipelines commonly encode these structural requirements in separately
maintained mapping logic, requiring coordinated updates to profiles and implementation. Existing approaches address different aspects of this problem. Redmatch¹
provides a dedicated mapping language for REDCap data, while FUME² and Sinaci et al. [2] support profile-aware transformations through custom mapping languages.
Marfoglia et al. [3] demonstrate a modular pipeline using manually authored FHIR StructureMaps. FML2Mirth [4] and MaLaC-HD [5] support execution of existing FHIR
Mapping Language (FML) definitions in other environments. Here we show that standardized, executable FHIR StructureMaps can be generated based on profile-
constraints while documenting unresolved source mappings. We evaluate the approach using controlled, synthetic, and real-world profiles and comparisons
independently developed pipelines. Secondary experiments investigate a feedback-guided agent repair.
